gloss: to be raised; to come up; to be cited

definitions.gloss: to be brought up; to be cited; to be named
definitions.explanation: Said of names, examples, opinions, or candidates that come up in a discussion. This kanji is the one used when something is put forward for consideration rather than physically rising.

definitions.gloss: to be produced; to be obtained (of results or evidence)
definitions.explanation: Said of results, profits, or evidence that come to hand as the product of effort or investigation.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}でいくつか{意見|いけん}が{挙|あ}がった。
examples.english: Several opinions were raised at the meeting.

examples.japanese: {候補|こうほ}として{三人|さんにん}の{名前|なまえ}が{挙|あ}がっているが、まだ{決|き}まっていない。
examples.english: Three names have come up as candidates, but nothing has been decided yet.

examples.japanese: {捜査|そうさ}で{新|あたら}しい{証拠|しょうこ}が{挙|あ}がった。
examples.english: New evidence came to light in the investigation.

examples.japanese: {時間|じかん}をかけた{割|わり}に{成果|せいか}が{挙|あ}がらず、{方法|ほうほう}を{見直|みなお}すことにした。
examples.english: Little came of it despite the time spent, so we decided to review our approach.

notes:
One of several kanji written for あがる. {挙|あ}がる is the transitive {挙|あ}げる's intransitive partner, used where something is put forward or produced.

CHOOSING THE KANJI:
- {上|あ}がる: to go up — the general word for rising
- {挙|あ}がる: to be cited, to be produced — names, examples, results, evidence
- {揚|あ}がる: to be deep-fried; to be hoisted

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {名前|なまえ}が{挙|あ}がる: a name comes up
- {例|れい}が{挙|あ}がる: an example is given
- {成果|せいか}が{挙|あ}がる: results are achieved
- {証拠|しょうこ}が{挙|あ}がる: evidence is obtained

TRANSITIVITY:
Intransitive; the thing raised is marked with が. The transitive partner is {挙|あ}げる ({例|れい}を{挙|あ}げる, to give an example).
